page: Microsoft Azure E2ads_v7 is an entry-level memory-optimized virtual machine running on Microsoft Hyper-V. The instance is built on the AMD EPYC 9V45 processor using the x86_64 architecture, operating at clock frequencies up to 4.5 GHz. It provides 2 dedicated vCPUs provisioned across 1 physical core with 2 execution threads, paired with 16.0 GB of system memory to maintain an 8.0 GB per vCPU ratio. Storage resources include a bundled 118 GB local NVMe SSD, while discrete GPU acceleration is absent. The CPU features support for advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 with VNNI and bfloat16, alongside hardware cryptographic acceleration.

Performance profiles reflect the distinction between its high-frequency single-thread capabilities and constrained core count. In single-threaded benchmarks, the instance demonstrates top-tier capability, generating 40.86 GB/sec in gzip compression and 18.15 GB/sec in bzip3 decompression, alongside top-decile single-core stress-ng results. In contrast, multi-core aggregate benchmarks such as the PassMark CPU score (5098.98) and multi-core stress-ng register in the bottom quartile due to the two-vCPU ceiling. Memory subsystem benchmarks show balanced uncached memory bandwidth of 43.73 GB/sec for reads and 33.33 GB/sec for writes, whereas high-concurrency throughput tests including Redis SET operations and static web serving place in the lower tier.

From a resource-efficiency standpoint, the E2ads_v7 trades wide multi-core scaling for high per-core execution speeds, substantial memory density, and low-latency local NVMe storage. This hardware balance makes the instance suitable for workloads that require strong per-thread processing and dedicated memory overhead without massive parallel concurrency, including small Redis or memcached instances, lightweight relational databases, single-worker data transformation jobs, and non-parallelized continuous integration tasks.
description: Microsoft Azure E2ads_v7 is a memory-optimized virtual machine powered by an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor capable of reaching 4.5 GHz on Microsoft Hyper-V. The system is configured with 2 dedicated vCPUs derived from 1 physical core, 16.0 GB of RAM, and a bundled 118 GB local NVMe SSD, without discrete GPUs. The x86_64 architecture includes AVX-512 vector and cryptographic instruction support. In benchmark evaluations, the instance demonstrates top-tier single-core performance and rapid compression speeds exceeding 40 GB/sec on gzip tests. Conversely, aggregate multi-core throughput and database transactions align with the lower quartile due to the 2-vCPU limit. Memory bandwidth tests yield mid-tier read and write rates around 43.73 GB/sec and 33.33 GB/sec respectively. This instance is best applied to memory-intensive, low-concurrency workloads such as small in-memory caches, development databases, and single-threaded batch data transformations.
